Map a survey export onto standardised concepts

Source: R/read.R
map_vcs_variables.Rd

Turns a raw wide or long export into a vcs_data object with separate household-, child- and vaccination-level tables. The raw import is carried along untouched.

map_vcs_variables(
  data,
  dictionary,
  schedule = NULL,
  keep_raw = TRUE,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, typically from read_vcs().

dictionary

A vcs_dictionary().

schedule

A vcs_schedule(). Required when the dictionary maps vaccine-level concepts.

keep_raw

Keep the untouched import inside the result. TRUE by default; set to FALSE for very large exports where memory matters, at the cost of losing the original-value column of the audit trail.

strict

Error when a mapped source column is absent from data. FALSE (default) warns and treats the column as all-missing.

Value

A vcs_data object.

Details

A child record is created wherever any of its mapped child-level or vaccine-level source columns holds a value, so empty repeat slots in a wide export do not become phantom children.

See also

validate_vcs(), vcs_dictionary()

Examples

dict <- vcs_dictionary(
  interview_id = "KEY", household_id = "KEY", psu = "psu",
  child_id = "child_{c}_{k}", card_seen = "card_{c}_{k}",
  card_status = "CVH{vv}_{c}_{k}", card_date = "CVH{vv}_date_{c}_{k}",
  n_caregivers = 1, n_children = 2
)
sched <- vcs_schedule_who(c("BCG", "PENTA1"))
raw <- data.frame(
  KEY = c("h1", "h2"), psu = c("P1", "P1"),
  child_1_1 = c("c1", "c3"), child_1_2 = c("c2", NA),
  card_1_1 = c("1", "1"), card_1_2 = c("0", NA),
  CVH01_1_1 = c("1", "1"), CVH01_date_1_1 = c("2024-01-05", "2024-02-01"),
  CVH02_1_1 = c("1", "3"), CVH02_date_1_1 = c("2024-03-05", NA),
  CVH01_1_2 = c("1", NA), CVH01_date_1_2 = c("2024-01-06", NA),
  CVH02_1_2 = c("3", NA), CVH02_date_1_2 = c(NA, NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
map_vcs_variables(raw, dict, sched)
#> <vcs_data>
#>   households  : 2
#>   children    : 3
#>   vaccinations: 6 rows (2 vaccine[s])
#>   raw import  : 2 x 14 (preserved)
#>   source      : NA
